Traupman 122
M-O s.v. furnished attic

1subtēgulāneum: long e (Lewis & Short sub-tĕgŭlānĕus, against its own tēgula). The word is built on tēgula, which Lewis & Short marks long (s.v. tēgulae); the ē of tēgula is kept.

subtēgulāneum1, subtēgulāneī n.

noun, second declension

attic, loft room

“Attic” is a modern application (Traupman). The ancient adjective’s sense is clear: Pliny, NH 36.185 has pavīmenta … barbarica atque subtēgulānea, floors under the roof, i.e. indoors (Lewis & Short: “that is under the roof, = in-doors”). An older Morgan draft called Pliny’s sense uncertain; the passage settles it.

Examples

  • conclāve sub tēctō

    a room under the roof, a loft roomcomposed

See also roof, ceiling, storey, top floor, knee wall.

SourcesLewis & Short: subtegulaneus · Morgan–Owens: furnished attic · Morgan–Owens: garret attic room · Older Morgan draft: attic caveat
